passage: I'm Sabina. In Class 6 I made a joke about Bhupen's old school bag, and half the class hooted. It felt like being lit up from inside. So I made another joke the next day, and another. But the cheering was thin. The moment I stopped, the same faces turned to their notebooks, and nobody asked me to sit with them at lunch. Bhupen never looked up at me at all; he ate alone by the window. That afternoon I understood that those claps had never meant respect. I stopped the jokes, and at lunch I offered him half my orange. He looked surprised and said thanks, very quietly.

qa.q: What did Sabina make a joke about?
qa.a: Sabina made a joke about Bhupen's old school bag.

qa.q: Why did Sabina stop making jokes about Bhupen?
qa.a: Sabina saw that the cheering was thin and faded once the jokes stopped, and understood it had never meant real respect.

qa.q: What did Sabina do after stopping the jokes, and why might it matter to Bhupen?
qa.a: Sabina offered him half an orange at lunch, a small kind step that showed him respect after the mockery.

qa.q: How might Bhupen have felt eating alone by the window while the class cheered the jokes?
qa.a: He was probably hurt and lonely, since he never looked up at Sabina and ate by himself.

grounding: A child mocks a classmate for the applause, sees the cheering is empty, and chooses respect.
